title: The investigation log request — question explanation
learningObjective: Use authorized logs and preserve relevant evidence without over-collecting personal data
format: 16:9 educational motion-graphics video; narration; separate captions; no autoplay with sound
visualStyle: Deep navy and charcoal; restrained cyan/electric-blue highlights; limited purple accents; clean typography; purposeful, low-motion transitions; accessible contrast.

scenes.name: Scenario setup
scenes.visual: During an investigation, a manager asks you to export all employee browsing history and personal messages, although the incident concerns access to one cloud folder.
scenes.direction: Show a fictional simulated setting. Use generic UI and no actual organization, brand, user identity, credential, real URL or live account.

scenes.name: Learning objective and risk cue
scenes.visual: Use authorized logs and preserve relevant evidence without over-collecting personal data
scenes.direction: Highlight only observable cues and explain the decision context without implying certainty beyond the scenario.

scenes.name: Recommended response
scenes.visual: Option C: Work with authorized investigators to identify relevant log sources, scope, retention and access controls; preserve integrity and document handling. Evidence collection should be authorized, relevant, minimized and handled with integrity.
scenes.direction: Animate the recommended defensive choice as a clear decision path. Display the action verb and trusted channel/control.

scenes.name: Why the other options fail
scenes.visual: Option A: Authorized, proportionate logs may be necessary for a legitimate investigation. Option B: Altering original evidence destroys integrity and undermines investigative reliability. Option D: Over-collection creates privacy, security and proportionality risks and may exceed the investigation’s authorization.
scenes.direction: Show each unsafe alternative separately with a complete, concise reason. Do not depict operational exploitation, malicious code or credential capture.

scenes.name: Defensive takeaway
scenes.visual: Confirm authority and scope, preserve source records, restrict access, record collection metadata and involve privacy/legal roles where required. Collect the minimum authorized evidence needed, preserve integrity and record chain of handling.
scenes.direction: Close with one readable takeaway and the next safe action. Keep the final frame long enough for comprehension.
scenes.onScreenText: Collect the minimum authorized evidence needed, preserve integrity and record chain of handling.

narration: Scenario: During an investigation, a manager asks you to export all employee browsing history and personal messages, although the incident concerns access to one cloud folder. Safest response: Option C: Work with authorized investigators to identify relevant log sources, scope, retention and access controls; preserve integrity and document handling. Evidence collection should be authorized, relevant, minimized and handled with integrity. Option A is unsafe because Authorized, proportionate logs may be necessary for a legitimate investigation. Option B is unsafe because Altering original evidence destroys integrity and undermines investigative reliability. Option D is unsafe because Over-collection creates privacy, security and proportionality risks and may exceed the investigation’s authorization. In practice: Confirm authority and scope, preserve source records, restrict access, record collection metadata and involve privacy/legal roles where required. Key takeaway: Collect the minimum authorized evidence needed, preserve integrity and record chain of handling.
